analysis.paper_title: Integrating Efficient Optimal Transport and Functional Maps For Unsupervised Shape Correspondence Learning
analysis.research_question: Can alternative optimal transport costs improve non-rigid shape correspondence?

objects.label: Equation 1
objects.title: Optimal functional map objective
objects.what_it_is: Optimization objective for functional map C combining data and regularization terms.
objects.why_it_is_here: Recaps functional map representation before introducing learning framework.
objects.claim_supported: Functional map solver recovers dense correspondence from learned features.
objects.limitations: Does not establish how features A,B are learned or which E_reg is used in implementation.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Foundational background for deep functional map module, but not novel contribution.

equation.role_in_method: Defines optimal functional map computation from descriptor coefficients; core solver used in pipeline.

objects.research_relevance: Recaps standard functional map optimization, not an OT cost; provides background context for correspondence but does not test alternative costs.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Background on functional maps, not OT.

objects.label: Equation 2
objects.title: Wasserstein distance definition
objects.what_it_is: Definition of p-Wasserstein distance as infimum over couplings.
objects.why_it_is_here: Introduces OT background and computational bottleneck.
objects.claim_supported: Wasserstein distance is accurate but O(m^3 log m) time and O(m^2) memory, motivating efficient OT.
objects.limitations: Does not give computable estimator; only definition and complexity discussion.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Background definition to contrast with proposed sliced OT loss.

symbols.meaning: set of couplings with marginals mu, nu

equation.role_in_method: Background OT metric; motivates need for sliced approximation due to cost.

objects.research_relevance: Defines baseline Wasserstein distance and its cubic cost, establishing what alternative OT costs must improve upon.

objects.label: Equation 3
objects.title: Sinkhorn / entropic regularized OT divergence
objects.what_it_is: Entropic-regularized OT objective with KL constraint and entropy term.
objects.why_it_is_here: Explains Sinkhorn alternative and its remaining quadratic cost.
objects.claim_supported: Entropic OT allows Sinkhorn solver in O(m^2) time but still quadratic memory and not a valid metric.
objects.limitations: Does not establish metric properties; paper notes triangle inequality fails.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Background for entropic OT used later only in refinement module.
objects.evidence: p.3, Eq.3 and Sinkhorn divergence paragraph

equation.role_in_method: Background regularized OT; later reused only for adaptive refinement, not training loss.

objects.research_relevance: Describes entropic-regularized Sinkhorn OT as one alternative cost with quadratic cost and non-metric limitation.

objects.label: Equation 4
objects.title: Sliced Wasserstein distance definition
objects.what_it_is: Expectation of 1D Wasserstein distances over random projections.
objects.why_it_is_here: Introduces fast valid OT metric adopted for unsupervised loss.
objects.claim_supported: Sliced Wasserstein provides O(n log n) time and O(n) memory valid OT metric.
objects.limitations: Definition alone does not give Monte Carlo implementation or how applied to mesh features.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Core efficient OT concept enabling novel losses; central to contribution.
objects.evidence: p.3, Eq.4 and Sliced Wasserstein paragraph

equation.role_in_method: Theoretical basis for proposed efficient OT loss; expectation over 1D projections with closed form.

objects.research_relevance: Defines sliced Wasserstein distance, the core efficient alternative OT metric proposed to improve correspondence.

objects.label: Equation 5
objects.title: Monte Carlo sliced Wasserstein estimator
objects.what_it_is: Finite-sample average of 1D Wasserstein distances.
objects.why_it_is_here: Shows how SW is computed efficiently in practice.
objects.claim_supported: SW can be approximated with L Monte Carlo projections.
objects.limitations: Does not address discriminativeness of uniform slicing; motivates EBSW.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Implementation detail for computing SW, supports proposed loss.

symbols.meaning: sampled projection directions from unit sphere

equation.role_in_method: Practical estimator for SW used in training.

objects.research_relevance: Gives Monte Carlo estimator making sliced Wasserstein tractable, enabling its use as a correspondence loss.

objects.label: Equation 6
objects.title: Energy-based sliced Wasserstein definition
objects.what_it_is: Expectation under energy-weighted slicing distribution.
objects.why_it_is_here: Introduces discriminative SW extension to motivate bidirectional loss.
objects.claim_supported: Energy-based slicing gives more discriminative SW variant.
objects.limitations: Original EBSW definition, not yet bidirectional formulation used in paper.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Basis for improved EBSW loss variant claimed as contribution.

symbols.meaning: energy-based slicing distribution proportional to f(W^p_p)

equation.role_in_method: Background for bidirectional EBSW loss; introduces energy-weighted slicing distribution.

objects.research_relevance: Defines energy-based sliced Wasserstein, a more discriminative alternative OT cost variant tested for correspondence.

objects.label: Equation 7
objects.title: Importance-sampling EBSW estimator
objects.what_it_is: Weighted average of 1D distances with normalized importance weights.
objects.why_it_is_here: Shows tractable computation of EBSW from proposal samples.
objects.claim_supported: EBSW can be computed via importance sampling with normalized weights.
objects.limitations: Generic estimator; not yet bidirectional shared distribution.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Supports implementation of EBSW but not final novel loss.
objects.evidence: p.4, Eq.7 and importance sampling paragraph

equation.role_in_method: Computational recipe for EBSW using proposal samples.

objects.research_relevance: Details importance-sampling estimator for EBSW, an implementation detail rather than the cost comparison itself.

objects.label: Equation 8
objects.title: Functional map structural loss
objects.what_it_is: Weighted sum of bijectivity and orthogonality penalties on C.
objects.why_it_is_here: Defines training objective for functional map module.
objects.claim_supported: Structural FM regularization promotes bijectivity and area preservation.
objects.limitations: Enforces intrinsic smoothness only; does not align extrinsic features explicitly.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Standard FM component combined with novel OT losses.

equation.role_in_method: Unsupervised FM regularizer term in total loss enforcing map structure.

objects.research_relevance: Defines bijectivity and orthogonality penalties for functional maps, unrelated to choice of OT cost.

objects.label: Equation 9
objects.title: Soft feature similarity matrix
objects.what_it_is: Row-softmax of feature dot-products giving soft correspondence matrix.
objects.why_it_is_here: Enables differentiable extrinsic alignment via OT.
objects.claim_supported: Softmax feature similarity provides differentiable proxy for correspondence.
objects.limitations: Soft assignment only; not guaranteed to be permutation or cycle-consistent alone.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Key bridge linking extractor features to OT and proper losses.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.9 and Soft feature similarity paragraph

symbols.meaning: d-dim feature of point i in X
d-dim feature of point j in Y

equation.role_in_method: Constructs soft permutation used to permute features for OT losses and proper loss.

objects.research_relevance: Creates differentiable soft correspondence from features that OT losses then align, supporting but not comparing OT costs.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Enabling similarity, not OT cost itself.

objects.label: Equation 10
objects.title: Bidirectional sliced Wasserstein loss
objects.what_it_is: Bidirectional SW discrepancy between Fx vs permuted Fy and vice versa.
objects.why_it_is_here: Proposes fast OT objective for explicit feature alignment.
objects.claim_supported: Bidirectional SW loss aligns feature distributions and encourages cycle consistency.
objects.limitations: Uses uniform slicing which may weight uninformative directions equally.
objects.paper_importance_reason: First novel OT loss; central claim of efficient OT for shape matching.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.10 and SW distance as efficient OT paragraph

equation.role_in_method: Novel unsupervised OT loss minimizing discrepancy between features and softly permuted counterpart.

objects.research_relevance: Proposes bidirectional sliced Wasserstein loss for explicit feature alignment, directly testing if SW improves correspondence.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Proposed alternative OT loss for matching.

objects.label: Equation 11
objects.title: Bidirectional energy-based SW loss
objects.what_it_is: Importance-sampled EBSW with slicing distribution shared by both directions.
objects.why_it_is_here: Improves over uniform SW by focusing on informative projections.
objects.claim_supported: Bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution improves over uniform SW.
objects.limitations: Requires importance sampling; added complexity vs vanilla SW, still needs empirical validation.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Second novel loss; claimed to be more discriminative and best performing.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.11 and Bidirectional EBSW paragraph

equation.role_in_method: More expressive OT loss weighting informative projection directions.

objects.research_relevance: Proposes bidirectional EBSW loss with shared slicing distribution, directly testing if energy-weighted SW further improves correspondence.

objects.label: Equation 12
objects.title: Proper functional map loss
objects.what_it_is: Squared error between Cxy and map induced by soft correspondence.
objects.why_it_is_here: Introduces coupling loss regularizing both FM and OT.
objects.claim_supported: Properness regularization couples functional map with OT similarity for smoothness and precision.
objects.limitations: Does not alone guarantee bijectivity; relies on joint optimization with other losses.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Links extrinsic OT alignment with intrinsic FM smoothness.
objects.evidence: p.5, Eq.12 and Proper functional maps paragraph

equation.role_in_method: Couples FM and soft pointwise map to enforce properness.

objects.research_relevance: Defines properness coupling between functional map and soft map, a smoothness regularizer not comparing OT costs.
objects.research_relevance_reason: About FM-OT coupling, not cost choice.

objects.label: Equation 13
objects.title: Total unsupervised loss
objects.what_it_is: Weighted sum of FM, OT, and proper losses.
objects.why_it_is_here: Summarizes training objective optimized end-to-end.
objects.claim_supported: Joint unsupervised training of FM, OT and proper terms yields precise smooth maps.
objects.limitations: Weights lambda need tuning; no supervision, performance depends on datasets.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Defines end-to-end unsupervised framework combining all components.
objects.evidence: p.6, Eq.13 and Total loss paragraph

symbols.meaning: OT loss either biSW or biEBSW

equation.role_in_method: Overall training objective where LOT is L_biSW or L_biEBSW.

objects.research_relevance: Sums FM, OT and proper terms into total training objective, showing joint use but not isolating OT cost effect.

objects.label: Equation 14
objects.title: Adaptive refinement via entropic OT
objects.what_it_is: Iterated Sinkhorn projections to obtain entropic OT plan.
objects.why_it_is_here: Defines per-pair refinement leveraging differentiability of Sinkhorn.
objects.claim_supported: Differentiable Sinkhorn refinement per pair improves final point map.
objects.limitations: Used only once at inference due to quadratic memory; not used for large-scale training.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Novel adaptive refinement module claimed to boost accuracy.

equation.role_in_method: Adaptive test-time refinement estimating pseudo soft correspondence via entropic OT.

objects.research_relevance: Defines test-time adaptive refinement via entropic OT Sinkhorn plan, another alternative OT cost improving final maps.

objects.label: Figure 1
objects.title: Overview of unsupervised shape matching via efficient OT
objects.what_it_is: Pipeline diagram showing feature extraction, FM solver, soft similarity and OT cost.
objects.why_it_is_here: Visualizes proposed joint learning framework.
objects.claim_supported: Framework combining DiffusionNet extractor, FM solver and OT cost achieves precise smooth maps.
objects.limitations: Schematic only; does not quantify performance or show refinement loop.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Central overview tying feature, FM and OT components together.

components: OT block with Pi-hat and Random Projections
flow: X Y -> Features Extractor -> Fx Fy
Fx Fy + Pi-hat -> OT cost -> Ltotal
figure.role_in_method: Illustrates end-to-end pipeline from shapes to point-to-point correspondence.

objects.research_relevance: Visualizes pipeline combining feature extractor, FM solver and OT cost, giving context for where alternatives plug in.

objects.label: Figure 2
objects.title: Qualitative results on SHREC19 texture transfer
objects.what_it_is: Checker-texture transfer comparison across methods.
objects.why_it_is_here: Demonstrates fewer artifacts vs baselines.
objects.claim_supported: Method yields better texture transfer on SHREC19 than Deep Shells and ULRSSM.
objects.limitations: Visual only; subjective and limited to few SHREC19 examples.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Supports near-isometric SOTA claim visually.

flow: Source texture -> transferred to target pose via each method

objects.research_relevance: Shows qualitative texture transfer gains on SHREC19, evidencing improved correspondence but not isolating which OT cost caused it.

objects.label: Figure 3
objects.title: Qualitative results on SMAL non-isometric matching
objects.what_it_is: Color-transfer comparison on animal shapes.
objects.why_it_is_here: Shows superior point mapping on non-isometric data.
objects.claim_supported: Method obtains precise smooth non-isometric maps where AFMap and ULRSSM fail.
objects.limitations: Few examples; does not isolate which loss causes improvement.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Visual support for challenging SMAL non-isometric claim.

flow: Source color map -> target animal via correspondence

objects.research_relevance: Shows qualitative non-isometric matching on SMAL animals, evidencing improvement without ablating OT costs.

objects.label: Figure 4
objects.title: Qualitative segmentation transfer results
objects.what_it_is: Coarse and fine-grained body segmentation transfer examples.
objects.why_it_is_here: Visualizes segmentation transfer capability without training segmentation model.
objects.claim_supported: Correspondence enables high-quality segmentation transfer close to ground truth.
objects.limitations: Qualitative; quantitative mIOU in Table 3 needed for claim.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Illustrates generalization to different mesh resolution and downstream use.

components: GT segmentation for coarse and fine-grained
flow: Source labels -> propagated via computed correspondence
figure.role_in_method: Downstream task validation of correspondence quality.

objects.research_relevance: Illustrates downstream body segmentation transfer, a different task that does not compare OT costs.

objects.label: Table 1
objects.title: Quantitative near-isometric shape matching
objects.what_it_is: Mean geodesic errors for FAUST, SCAPE, SHREC19 under three training regimes.
objects.why_it_is_here: Benchmarks against axiomatic, supervised, unsupervised baselines.
objects.claim_supported: Method outperforms axiomatic, supervised and unsupervised baselines in most near-isometric settings.
objects.limitations: Mean geodesic error only; best/second-best coloring does not give variance or significance.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Primary quantitative proof of near-isometric SOTA including SHREC19.

important_comparisons: Ours 1.5 vs ULRSSM 1.6 on FAUST-trained FAUST; Ours 5.5 second-best on FAUST-trained SHREC19
Ours 1.6/1.8/7.0 and 1.6/2.2/4.7 on SCAPE and FAUST+SCAPE splits beating Deep Shells and AFMap
table.result_interpretation: Ours best or second-best in most train/test splits; supervised overfit, unsupervised generalizes.

objects.research_relevance: Reports SOTA geodesic errors on FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19, showing overall method with efficient OT improves near-isometric correspondence.

objects.label: Table 2
objects.title: Quantitative non-isometric matching on SMAL and DT4D-H
objects.what_it_is: Geodesic errors comparing Deep Shells, GeoFMaps, AFMap, ULRSSM, Ours.
objects.why_it_is_here: Validates method on non-isometric animal/humanoid data.
objects.claim_supported: Method surpasses SOTA on challenging SMAL and DT4D-H non-isometric sets.
objects.limitations: Only intra-class DT4D-H tested; limited baselines listed.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Key evidence for non-isometric generalization, core contribution.

important_comparisons: Ours 4.0 vs ULRSSM 4.2 vs AFMap 5.4 on SMAL
Ours 4.2 vs ULRSSM 4.5 vs AFMap 11.6 on DT4D-H
table.result_interpretation: Ours lowest error on both datasets, establishing new SOTA.

objects.research_relevance: Reports SOTA errors on SMAL and DT4D-H, showing efficient OT method improves challenging non-isometric correspondence.

objects.label: Table 3
objects.title: Quantitative 3D shape segmentation transfer
objects.what_it_is: mIOU for coarse and fine-grained segmentation transfer.
objects.why_it_is_here: Evaluates downstream co-segmentation performance.
objects.claim_supported: Correspondence-based transfer sets new SOTA for 3D segmentation without segmentation training.
objects.limitations: Trained on FAUST_r 10K faces, tested on 20K faces; mIOU only, no per-class breakdown.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Demonstrates downstream utility and discretization-agnostic generalization.

table.result_interpretation: Ours highest on both coarse (4 classes) and fine-grained (17 classes).

objects.research_relevance: Reports mIOU for segmentation transfer, a downstream application unrelated to comparing OT costs.

objects.label: Table 4
objects.title: Ablation study on SHREC19
objects.what_it_is: Ablation over OT loss variants and adaptive refinement.
objects.why_it_is_here: Validates design choices for feature alignment and refinement.
objects.claim_supported: BiSW/EBSW and adaptive refinement each improve over MSE and no-refinement.
objects.limitations: Trained on FAUST+SCAPE, tested only on SHREC19; does not separate biEBSW number in table body beyond text.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Directly isolates contribution of OT loss choice and refinement.

table.metric: Mean geodesic error x100 on SHREC19
table.result_interpretation: MSE fails to align; bidirectional SW slightly beats uniSW; refinement gives large gain.

objects.research_relevance: Ablates MSE vs BiSW/EBSW and refinement on SHREC19, directly answering whether alternative OT costs improve correspondence.

objects.title: SOTA near-isometric shape correspondence
objects.what_it_is: Experimentally testable claim that method outperforms prior axiomatic/supervised/unsupervised baselines on remeshed FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19.
objects.why_it_is_here: Summarizes primary empirical contribution for near-isometric scenario.
objects.claim_supported: Proposed unsupervised EOT+FM method achieves SOTA near-isometric matching (FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19).
objects.limitations: Not stated whether gains are statistically significant; limited to mean geodesic error.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Central performance claim covering main human shape benchmarks.
objects.evidence: p.6-7, Sec.5.1 text plus Table 1 and Fig.2
objects.research_relevance: Claims SOTA near-isometric matching with EOT+FM, providing empirical yes to improvement but without cost-wise breakdown.

objects.title: SOTA non-isometric matching and transfer
objects.what_it_is: Claim of superior geodesic error on SMAL/DT4D-H and higher mIOU on FAUST segmentation transfer.
objects.why_it_is_here: Captures generalization beyond near-isometric humans.
objects.claim_supported: Proposed method achieves SOTA non-isometric matching (SMAL/DT4D-H) and segmentation transfer.
objects.limitations: Does not establish cross-dataset training details beyond splits from [16]; resolution differs (10K vs 20K).
objects.paper_importance_reason: Extends SOTA claim to harder non-isometric and downstream tasks showing generalization.
objects.evidence: p.7-8, Sec.5.2-5.3 text plus Table 2, Table 3, Fig.3, Fig.4
objects.research_relevance: Claims SOTA non-isometric matching and segmentation transfer, supporting generalization but not isolating OT cost effect.

objects.title: OT loss and refinement efficacy
objects.what_it_is: Claim that replacing LOT with MSE degrades drastically and removing refinement degrades 4.7 to 7.2.
objects.why_it_is_here: Justifies novel components as causal drivers of performance.
objects.claim_supported: Bidirectional SW/EBSW OT loss and entropic adaptive refinement are necessary for best accuracy.
objects.limitations: Ablation only on SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training; does not ablate proper or fmap weights.
objects.paper_importance_reason: Mechanistic claim attributing gains to proposed OT losses and refinement.
objects.research_relevance: Claims replacing OT loss with MSE degrades drastically and refinement helps, directly attributing gains to alternative OT costs.
objects.research_relevance_reason: Causal claim for OT loss efficacy.
